Section: Full Flow: Admin User Management → App Config → Quote
Test Steps:
1. Admin logs into admin portal and verifies /users
2. Admin checks /applications to view all apps
3. Engineering logs into test web portal
4. Engineering navigates to /installation-system
5. Engineering selects a solution (A210)
6. Engineering opens comparison and configures options
7. Engineering views configuration summary
Expected Result: Admin can see all users and applications. Engineering can complete the full configurator flow: filter → select → compare → configure → view summary.

Section: Full Flow: Create Application → Auto-Filter → Configure
Precondition: User is logged in as engineering
Test Steps:
1. Login as engineering on test web portal
2. Navigate to /installation-system
3. Record initial match count
4. Click "Setup New Application"
5. Fill name="Demo App", volume=100000, material="Steel"
6. Click "Save"
7. Verify filters auto-updated
8. Select matching solution (from filtered list)
9. Click "Compare / Configure Solutions"
10. Click "Configure Solution"
11. Add a machine option to configuration
12. Observe portfolio totals updated
Expected Result: App created successfully. Filters auto-set based on app. Solutions filtered. Config panel shows options. Portfolio updated. Full end-to-end flow works.

Section: Full Flow: Multi-App Portfolio → Configure Two Solutions
Precondition: User is logged in as engineering
Test Steps:
1. Login and go to /installation-system
2. Create "App Alpha" with volume=80000
3. Create "App Beta" with volume=120000
4. Verify portfolio shows total 200,000
5. Select solution A210 and 824 eDrive
6. Compare and configure both
7. Navigate between config panels
Expected Result: Portfolio combines both apps. Multiple solutions can be compared. Configuration works for each solution independently.

Section: Full Flow: Use Existing App → Modify → Regenerate
Test Steps:
1. Login as engineering
2. Navigate to /installation-system
3. Click "Use Existing Application"
4. Select a previously created app
5. Click OK to load it
6. Edit the app - change volume
7. Save and observe portfolio update
8. Select solution and configure
Expected Result: Existing app loads correctly. Editing updates portfolio. Configuration flow works with loaded app data.

Section: Full Flow: Save Configuration → Return Later
Test Steps:
1. Login as engineering
2. Create an app, select solution, configure options
3. Sign out
4. Login again as engineering
5. Navigate to /installation-system
6. Load same app via Use Existing
7. Select same solution and configure
Expected Result: User can complete the flow across sessions. Previously saved apps persist. Configuration state may or may not persist (document behavior).

Section: Cross-Portal: Admin Creates User → Engineering Uses App
Test Steps:
1. Admin logs in, navigates to /users
2. Admin verifies engineering user exists
3. Engineering logs into test web portal
4. Engineering creates an application
5. Admin logs in again, navigates to /applications
6. Admin can see engineering's application
Expected Result: Admin can see all applications across users. Application created by engineering is visible in admin's /applications page.

Section: Flow: Negative - Access Without Login Any Page
Test Steps:
1. Clear all browser data
2. Try accessing: /installation-system
3. Try accessing: / (test web home)
4. Try accessing: /login (should work)
5. Try accessing admin: /users
6. Try accessing admin: /roles
Expected Result: All protected pages redirect to /login. Only /login is accessible without authentication.

Section: Flow: Negative - Rapid Login Attempts (Brute Force)
Precondition: User is on admin login page
Test Steps:
1. Navigate to admin /login
2. Attempt login 5+ times rapidly with invalid credentials
3. Observe behavior after repeated failures
Expected Result: After multiple failed attempts, either: account is temporarily locked, CAPTCHA appears, increasing delay introduced, or error message changes. Rate limiting is in place.

Section: Flow: Edge - Concurrent Sessions Same User
Test Steps:
1. Login as engineering in Browser A (tab 1)
2. Login as engineering in Browser B (tab 2, different browser/context)
3. Perform actions in both sessions
Expected Result: Both sessions allow concurrent access. OR second login invalidates first session. Document the behavior.

Section: Flow: Edge - All Filter Combinations Maximal
Test Steps:
1. Select all 4 element types
2. Check both capabilities
3. Set force range to full (21-300)
4. Observe matching count
Expected Result: All filters are active simultaneously. Count shows intersection of all criteria. UI renders correctly with all filters active.

Section: Flow: Edge - Maximum Solutions Selected
Test Steps:
1. Select as many solutions as the UI allows (try selecting all 47)
2. Click Compare / Configure Solutions
3. Observe comparison cards
Expected Result: UI handles large selection gracefully. Comparison cards display within viewport. Scrolling works if needed.

Section: Flow: Edge - Edit App Name While Solutions Configured
Precondition: User has app loaded and configured
Test Steps:
1. Create app "Original Name"
2. Select solution and configure options
3. Edit the app and rename to "Updated Name"
4. Save and observe
Expected Result: App card updates to new name. Configuration and solution selections are preserved. No data loss from renaming.

Section: Flow: Edge - Delete App While Configured
Precondition: User has app loaded and configured
Test Steps:
1. Create an app
2. Select solution and configure
3. Remove the app via Remove button
4. Observe configuration state
Expected Result: App is removed. Configuration panel may close or solution selection resets. No orphaned state.

Section: Flow: All 4 Roles Complete Basic Flow
Test Steps:
1. Login as Engineering: create app, select solution, configure
2. Login as Customer: select solution, view options
3. Login as Distributor: select solution, view options
4. Login as Sales: select solution, configure, view pricing
Expected Result: Each role can complete their authorized flow. No role experiences errors for authorized actions.

Section: Flow: Admin Logs Out → Other User Logs In
Test Steps:
1. Login as admin on admin portal
2. Sign out
3. Login as engineering on admin portal (not test web)
4. Navigate to /applications
5. Verify engineering's dashboard
Expected Result: Session from admin is properly terminated. Engineering can login independently. No session leakage between users.

Section: Flow: Mobile - Responsive Installation System
Test Steps:
1. Simulate mobile viewport (375x812 iPhone)
2. Login as engineering
3. Navigate to /installation-system
4. Attempt to: select filter, choose solution, compare
Expected Result: Page renders for mobile. Filters may collapse. Solutions grid stacks vertically. User can complete basic flow on mobile.

Section: Flow: Tab Switch - Filters Persist Across Navigation
Test Steps:
1. Apply filters (PEM selected, force 50-150)
2. Without deselecting, navigate to another browser tab
3. Switch back to installation system tab
Expected Result: Filters remain applied when returning to the tab. No session loss on tab switch.

Section: Flow: Browser Refresh - App State Preserved
Precondition: User has app loaded and solutions selected
Test Steps:
1. Create app, select solutions
2. Refresh browser (F5/Cmd+R)
3. Observe page state
Expected Result: App remains loaded. Solutions remain selected. Page state is preserved after refresh (state stored in session or fetched from server).

Section: Flow: Performance - Installation System Load Time
Test Steps:
1. Start timer
2. Login as engineering
3. Navigate to /installation-system
4. Measure time until all elements visible
Expected Result: Page loads within acceptable time (< 5 seconds for full load, < 3 seconds for interactive). No long loading spinners.

Section: Flow: Admin Analytics - Data Reflects Test Web Activity
Test Steps:
1. Engineering uses test web portal (creates apps, configures)
2. Admin navigates to /analytics on admin portal
3. Observe analytics data
Expected Result: Analytics dashboard shows metrics that include engineering's activity (total apps, sessions, etc.). Data is consistent between portals.
